utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is the case number, IT-04-74-PT, the Prosecutor versus Jadranko Prlic, Bruno Stojic, Slobodan Praljak, Milovoj Petkovic, Valentin Coric, and Berislav Pusic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. May I have the appearances. Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the Prosecution wants to be heard, it must switch on the microphone, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Kenneth Scott for the Prosecution, together with Josee D'Aoust, Pieter Kruger, Virginia De Abajo-Marques, and our case manager, Denise Gustin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Scott. For the Defence. Could I -- yes, let's go by the row.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Michael Karnavas for Dr. Prlic, and with me is Ms. Suzana Tomanovic. She's the co-counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Berislav Zivkovic, attorney-at-law from Zagreb, for the accused Bruno Stojic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zivkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Bozidar Kovacic as defence counsel for Mr. Slobodan Praljak. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Vesna Alaburic, Defence counsel for Milivoj Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Tomislav Jonjic, Defence counsel for Valentin Coric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon, learned friends. Appearing for Berislav Pusic, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, attorney-at-law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. We have a Status Conference in the case against Mr. Prlic and others. We have prepared an agenda. Are you informed about the agenda? The first item on the agenda is the status of negotiations on the Prosecution's proposed adjudicated and agreed facts. The second issue is pending motions. The third one is the work plan. And four is other issues. Would you like to add anything to the agenda? But you could also include them under "other issues." Then we'll start with the status of the negotiations on the Prosecution's proposed adjudicated and agreed facts. I am informed that at the 65 ter meeting that a time plan was agreed, and I already indicate that the Chamber grants the extension of time requested within the limits of the time plan agreed. The work plan will be distributed soon. Is there anything else you'd like to address in relation to the status of the negotiations of the proposed adjudicated and agreed facts?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, other than to say that that's absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So that we're all in agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the second issue - I'll just go by it one by one - the pending motions, second on the list of the agenda. The two motions that are pending, not only long but already too long, and I apologise for the Chamber that we have not given decisions yet. At the same time, you'll be aware that it's a rather complicated matter and that we would not like to rush through it but to give thorough decisions. These are the preliminary motions on the form of the indictment and the challenge of jurisdiction. Any observations in respect of that, apart from, perhaps, that I hope that you accept the apologies of the Chamber. If there's nothing there, then the next one is the request for variations of conditions of provisional release. There are two motions pending, the Coric fourth request and the -- for variation of the conditions of provisional release filed the 21st of June, and the Stojic request for variation of conditions of provisional release filed the 23rd of June. The Chamber expects to give a decision next week. We -- the Chamber has received the position of the Prosecution in that respect. Any further observations to be made in that respect? Then there are two motions for review of the Deputy Registrar's decision regarding a request for assignment of counsel: One filed on behalf of Mr. Praljak, one filed on behalf of Mr. Petkovic. We have not yet received the response by the Registry, and it is of utmost importance to have a response from the Registry because that sheds light on all the information exchanged between -- between counsel for Mr. Praljak and counsel for Mr. Petkovic. We could not expect any decision to be given before the recess. You'll understand that. I think under the -- although it might not be directly applicable, the Rule that a response should be received within two weeks, the Registry has been informed that if they want to respond - and Chamber very much want the Registry to respond - that the response should be received, I think, by next Thursday. That's the 21st of July. The Chamber is aware of the concerns it raises. At the same time, it's again not a matter which you could just deal with in a few seconds, especially since there are some -- I would say some matters of principle involved as well, especially the issue of whether information asked for by the Registry could cover only the present situation -- well, to say today and not yesterday. That is a matter which needs thorough consideration. Is there anything to be raised in this respect? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know whether it would be appropriate now or put -- or I can raise it under item -- whatever you say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it's about these motions, you may raise the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: We -- we have been told that the -- that the Chamber may decide to invite the accused to the hearing which possibly may be scheduled related to those motions you just mentioned, review of the Registry decision. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: -- if that -- if you will consider that, I would just like to put two or three facts which you, I think, might have -- want to have in mind in that decision. First, in a very similar situation which I faced personally in Kordic/Cerkez trial during the appeal phase, Judge Schomburg in a similar situation also set up a hearing, and despite of the fact that the client was here in Detention Unit, he was not invited. Second, if you decide to call the clients -- the accused to be present, that, of course, would imply relatively a lot of logistical issues and, of course, expenses as well. So if I may suggest, if Your Honour would believe that it would be appropriate to have the client here, perhaps a videolink conference could be also discussed and/or alternatively, if you anyhow decided that you would like to have the clients here on that hearing, then at least, if the circumstances will allow it, to have a hearing scheduled for afternoon sometime, not before 2.00 p.m., so we can organise a flight in a way that they stay here only one night, so we've minimised the whole -- the whole project. That is our submission, and I think I have also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understand also for Mr. Petkovic, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber, not having received yet the response by the Registrar, has not yet considered whether a hearing at all would be needed. There are several options. One of them is to put additional questions to the Registry and to the Defence to receive further information. There are a few issues -- for example, the matter of principle, whether you have to provide information only relevant today or also relevant yesterday is, of course, a matter -- mainly a legal matter, I would say, which would not require the presence of the accused themselves. If there would be any specific reason -- because I take it that we'll be -- it will be a lot of paperwork. I take it that we get the results of investigations made and we get copies of the requests for further information, the responses to such requests. I mean, for that reason I think also the presence of the accused would not be required. At the same time, if there are any specific reasons why the presence of Mr. Praljak and Mr. Petkovic would be needed in the view of the Defence, then we'd like to -- to be informed about that so that we can take a decision, if there would be a hearing, whether the presence of the accused would be required. So therefore we'd then like to -- it could be that they could give additional information, but it's hard to say for us at this moment where we have not even received the response by the Registry. Any further matter to be raised in this respect? But I noted that you at least want to consider us seriously to invite the accused. So my first response is: Give us the specific reasons what that should add to what counsel could say. I'm not saying it would not, but we'd like to know exactly. And then, of course, logistics, expenses, and the time of the hearing will be taken into consideration. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may clarify, Your Honour. My colleague Mr. Kovacic and I did not feel that the presence of our clients was indispensable in order to clarify all the facts pertaining to the decision on financing. My colleague Mr. Kovacic's comment referred mainly to the information we received at today's 65 ter conference that the possibility of our clients being invited to the hearing is not to be excluded. Should this happen, we submit that it might be organised in the way we suggested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand. So you do not take -- you just took into consideration that the Chamber might decide that the presence of the accused would be needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. Yes, that is exactly what you said. If the Chamber decides so, we are here. And by the way, I'm sure that if -- if the Chamber decides to -- to have a hearing, that I am capable, of course, with the -- with the help of my assistant, who is dedicated to the task, I could -- I'm sure I could answer any specific question in -- even in detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So -- thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you'd say you're fully informed about any factual --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- element that might come into play.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Kovacic and Ms. Alaburic. Then I'd like to move to the next matter, which is the work plan. The work plan covers at this moment when 65 ter meetings will be held. The next one -- I see the 27th of July. Is that correct, or is that a mistake? I see it here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I strike out one day and I do understand that on Wednesday, the 7th of September at 3.00 p.m., the next 65 ter meeting will be held. The next Status Conference is scheduled for the 17th of November of this year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps it's better to -- to distribute the list as soon as possible. It covers the disclosure of material. It also covers agreement on facts, the number of exhibits and witnesses, and the hours for the examination-in-chief and cross-examination of witnesses. It also deals with the Prosecution's motions to admit witnesses' statements under Rule 92 bis - I know that some progress has been made already in that respect - and when the pre-trial briefs should be filed. No date has been set for that; however, I take it that the Defence and the Prosecution is fully aware that the case is expected and is scheduled to start on from the 1st of December of this year. Then the work plan will be distributed. If there's anything to be submitted in this respect, you have an opportunity to do so now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Just by way of clarification. Your Honour, in the meeting today I believe it was agreed that the parties would next meet with Mr. Harhoff in terms of adjudicated facts on Thursday, the 8th of September at 2.00 in the afternoon, and it may be that it might not make sense to meet both on the 7th for the 65 ter and then on again the next day, although we could certainly combine those into possibly one session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It's not a major point. I'm sure all of us would be happy to be here on both days, but just by way of clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that it's scheduled for the 8th. Yes. Any further matters in relation to the work plan? If not, I come to the following point on the agenda, and that is other issues. Are there other issues? Of course, one of the usual issues to be discussed, but I'll rather keep that for last, is the health situation of the accused, and there the parties, of course, could -- could apply for private session. But apart from the health of the accused, is there any other issue to be raised at this moment? Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Not for the Prosecution, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I do have one issue that I wish to raise. I did raise it earlier during the 65 ter meeting, both yesterday and today, and it regards the Rule 45 motion filed by my client back in September last year. Now that we have a trial date, which is coming right upon us, and there's a lot of work to be done, and after being told by the Prosecutor how much -- how many hours they had to put in and resources expended to put together their -- these agreed facts and adjudicated facts, I think it is very clear that the Defence needs adequate resources, at least with respect to Dr. Prlic. So far we've been waiting patiently from the Registrar, but it's coming to a point where I think it's -- it's unbecoming of the UN to expect the Defence counsel to be subsidising the defence of their client. So I would most appreciate it if the Trial Chamber could perhaps apply - I don't want to say pressure - but sort of make some suggestions that they act upon it with all deliberate speed, as it were. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Karnavas, you were speaking on behalf of Mr. Prlic. Would this extend to any of the other accused? We -- I noticed already, I think, that the -- for Mr. Praljak and for Mr. Petkovic that we are -- that there is a decision by the Registrar and that we have to consider that once we've received the response by the Registry. Is there any similar concern valid for Mr. Stojic, Mr. Coric, or Mr. Pusic?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the situation is exactly the same in the case of Mr. Coric.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the same situation obtains in the case of Mr. Stojic, and in fact it is even more serious than in the other cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence of Mr. Pusic has received a decision. It has no objections in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So it's -- at this moment, the request for review are pending for Mr. Praljak and Mr. Petkovic, also Mr. Prlic, Mr. Coric, and Mr. Stojic. You would like to Chamber to urge the Registry to come up with a decision not only soon but even very soon. I will address the matter -- I'll take up the matter with the Registry. Any other other issue? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes. If I may, Your Honour. Since you raised the issue of the health of the accused and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But as I said before, I'd first like to deal with any other matters --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- apart from the health. But if there is nothing, then it is the right time to raise the issue. I'm looking around. I see no other other matters raised, so then time. Please proceed, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I apologise for jumping in front but I thought that nobody has anything to add. Well, you mentioned the issue of the health of the accused, and I believe that I ought to inform you that I will next week file a supplemental motion for variation of conditions of provisional release of my client. First of all, I'm grateful and thank the Chamber to -- already to grant my earlier motion where we asked approval for him to move down there in Dalmatia in order -- primarily in order to fix his stomatological problems because he has a brother there who is a dentist, and because of his lacking means, he's trying to do that on most economical way, of course. In the meantime, this situation is becoming much worse and much more serious than he believed, and he has just visited specialists in Zagreb and it is said that it is quite a serious problem; it will need about at least two months to fix a minimal problem, which is now really, really active. Well, that -- that raises many problems for my client and for myself because of cooperating in Defence. Nevertheless, I will file a motion -- a supplemental motion requesting probably additional time in Makarska but there might be other solutions as well. But what I'm trying to tell here is not only to inform you that we will do so, so not to surprise you tomorrow with a brand new motion, but also that primarily my client decided to finally solve this problem of his health in order to be fit for trial, because there really is a great possibility that when he will be back here in detention the problem may arise and be much more serious and complicated, causing some delays or his not appearing on the trial, et cetera. So we will do our best to fix that, but we are also looking for support from the Chamber if there will be need to do at least part of the work which have to be done, that they are done in Makarska because of economical reasons. I will, of course, explain all that in detail in the submission. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In order to make it possible for the Prosecution to respond to such a motion, I would very much like attached to the motion, I would say, the work plan from the dentist and a clear description of what exactly has to be done and how, in what stages it can be performed, and for how long the patient then should be present on -- on a more continuous basis; would that be for one week and then one or two weeks off? And so I'd like -- I'd like to receive for the Chamber as full as possible information. We also, then, are in a position, apart from treatment to be provided by a family member dentist -- we're also in a position to assess and ask even advice for that, to assess what consequences it might have at later stages if, for example, half of the treatment would be done, what risks that would result in for the trial, the risk of absence at trial. So therefore we'd like to have as complete as possible medical documentation on the exact problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You will have it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. Is there any other health issue to be raised? And as I said before, if you want to apply for private session, I certainly will consider it, because health is a private matter. Yes, Mr. Ibrisimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I believe we are still in private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are not in. I said you could apply for private session. But perhaps for the dentist, it's -- it's less sensitive than perhaps other problems. I don't know what's still to come. But Mr. Ibrisimovic, if -- if you'd --

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask that we go into private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In private session we've heard further details on health problems. Since I just asked you still in private session whether there were any other issues to be raised and the answer was no, this concludes the Status Conference. We'll adjourn sine die.
